latest_findings.claim: The second identical rerun of the N=256, 3000-step config reproduces the earlier rerun (exp-20261013-031820-91ca) exactly. Every probe trajectory value matches at all 7 checkpoints for force, accel_step, distance and energy: margin, best layer and R2 are identical to 3 decimals. Final best-layer margins match: force 0.113 (layer 1, R2 0.644 vs control 0.531) in seed 20 and 0.003 (layer 3, R2 0.586 vs control 0.583) in seed 21. accel_step is 0.162 (R2 0.926 vs control 0.765) in seed 20 and 0.198 (R2 0.912 vs control 0.714) in seed 21. So training and probing are deterministic for a fixed seed under the current pipeline, and accel_step clearly beats its control in both seeds while force beats it only in seed 20.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds match the earlier rerun with zero difference to the 3 decimals reported, which is far inside the 0.01 tolerance. The step-3000 val_mse_ratio values (0.237 and 0.282) could not be checked against the earlier rerun's, because that run's val_mse_ratio trajectory is not in the related-experiment data. The probe agreement makes a mismatch unlikely, but this part of the expected-if-true criterion is unverified here. Determinism is shown only within the current pipeline version, on one machine and one config. It says nothing about why the original pre-change N=256 runs (f-20261013-000253-c709) differ, which still points to a change in pipeline or controls. Two consequences follow. First, the step-3000 differences between the 3000-, 6000- and 12000-step N=256 runs (up to about 0.025 on force) must come from the lr-schedule horizon, not from noise. Second, the 0.11 force gap between seeds 20 and 21 is real seed-to-seed variance, not rerun noise. Any nonzero difference in a further identical rerun, or on different hardware, would weaken this.

latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 1, the force margin falls from N=64 to N=128 in both seeds, as predicted. At N=128 the final best-layer force margin is 0.137 for seed 20 (layer 1, R2 0.661 vs control 0.524) and 0.145 for seed 21 (layer 3, R2 0.662 vs control 0.517). The paired N=64 data_seed 1 runs both end at 0.209, so the drops are 0.072 and 0.064. The force controls are about the same in both arms (N=64 about 0.53, N=128 0.52), so the drop is in the trained force R2 (0.736-0.742 down to 0.661-0.662), not in the control. accel_step is essentially unchanged: R2 0.932/0.935 vs control 0.774/0.765, a raw margin of 0.158/0.170 and a headroom-normalised margin of 0.70/0.72, against 0.72/0.74 at N=64. Normalised force is only 0.29/0.30. Both N=128 runs beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.099/0.088).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds meet every expected-if-true criterion: force margin in [0.06, 0.20], at least 0.04 below the same seed's N=64 value, and normalised accel_step in [0.60, 0.78]. Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps. Three things limit confidence. (1) The drop on data_seed 1 (0.064-0.072) is smaller than on data_seed 0 (about 0.10-0.14), so the effect replicates in direction but its size depends on the dataset. Only two seeds and two datasets have been tested. (2) The N=128 force margin is still rising at step 3000 (seed 20: +0.007 per 500 steps; seed 21: +0.002). Earlier long runs showed the N=64-to-N=128 gap narrowing slowly, so this result describes the gap at a fixed 3000 steps, not at convergence. (3) Force is best at layer 1 in seed 20 but layer 3 in seed 21, so the best layer is not stable. The verdict would change if a third seed on data_seed 1, or another data_seed, gave an N=128 force margin within 0.02 of its paired N=64 value, or if longer training closed the gap.

latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 1 at N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, best-of-3 controls), both seeds match the data_seed 0 N=64 pattern. Final best-layer force margin is 0.209 in both seeds (layer 1; R2 0.736/0.742 vs control 0.527/0.534), and the accel_step margin is 0.157/0.162 (layer 4; R2 0.940/0.943 vs control 0.783/0.780). Headroom-normalised, accel_step is 0.725/0.740 and force 0.44/0.45, so force leads on raw margin while accel_step leads on normalised margin. val_mse_ratio is 0.0184/0.0176.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Every expected-if-true criterion is met in both seeds. Force is >= 0.18 with beats_control true, normalised accel_step is inside [0.60, 0.78], and val_mse_ratio is < 0.05. Force control spread is small (0.020/0.004), so the force margin clears the bar well. Caveats: (1) The force margin of 0.209 sits just below data_seed 0's 0.215-0.261 range. That gap is smaller than the data_seed 0 seed-to-seed spread, but with only 2 seeds here we cannot say whether data_seed 1 runs slightly lower. (2) Force is still rising at step 3000, by about +0.004 to +0.008 per 500 steps, so the comparison depends on training length. (3) The final force best layer is layer 1, which is also the distance layer (distance margin 0.685/0.574). Earlier, seed 21 beat control at layer 4 (margin 0.152 at step 1000), so force is not obviously confined to the distance layer, but no residualised force target was run. (4) formed_at_step for force is 1000 in both runs, but the trajectory margins are already >= 0.1 from step 500 (0.106 at layer 3 and 0.118 at layer 4). This repeats the earlier formed_at_step lag and only affects timing, not the verdict. A third seed below 0.15, or a data_seed 2 arm below 0.15, would turn this into dataset dependence. In the paired N=128 data_seed 1 arm (exp-20261013-051930-fcbc), force is 0.137/0.145 and normalised accel_step about 0.70/0.72. That puts the per-seed N=64 to N=128 force drop at about 0.064-0.072, against about 0.10-0.14 on data_seed 0. This finding is context only; the N=128 runs are not cited as evidence here.

latest_findings.claim: On fresh seeds 22-23 at N=128 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the final best-layer force margin is 0.108 (seed 22, layer 1, R2 0.569 vs control 0.461) and 0.094 (seed 23, layer 1, R2 0.562 vs control 0.468). That is 0.139-0.140 below the matched N=64 seeds (0.247/0.234) and well above N=256 (0.033-0.040). Seed 23 never reaches the 0.1 bar, and seed 22 crosses it only at step 2500. accel_step is decoded much better: layer-4 R2 0.894/0.898 vs controls 0.677/0.725, giving raw margins 0.217/0.174 and headroom-normalised margins 0.67/0.63, against about 0.68/0.71 at N=64. Force's normalised margin is only about 0.20/0.18.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both completed seeds meet every expected-if-true condition. Force is in [0.08, 0.20] and at least 0.04 below the same seed's N=64 value, and normalised accel_step is in [0.62, 0.77], so the gradual decline of force with steps_per_orbit replicates on new seeds. Caveats: (1) Both values sit near the low end of the predicted band and below seeds 20-21 at N=128 (0.150/0.131). With 4 seeds the N=128 range is 0.094-0.150, and seed 23 would not count as a beats-control force result on its own. A seed below 0.08 or above 0.20 in further N=128 runs would weaken the 'intermediate' claim. (2) The force drop comes from lower trained R2 (0.56-0.57 vs 0.68-0.70 at N=64), not from higher controls (0.46-0.47 vs about 0.45). This makes it a real decodability difference, but the force signal still sits at layer 1, the distance layer, and has not been tested with distance regressed out. (3) Force is still rising at step 3000 (about +0.004-0.006 per 500 steps, val_mse_ratio 0.067-0.079), so the N=64 vs N=128 gap holds only at matched training length. (4) Normalised accel_step is a little lower at N=128 (0.63-0.67) than at N=64 (0.68-0.71). That fits the predicted range, but 'flat across N' would be in doubt if more seeds widen this gap.

latest_findings.claim: At N=64, 12000 steps of training end with best-layer force margins of 0.255 (seed 20) and 0.266 (seed 21), both at layer 1, the distance layer. That is 0.062 and 0.069 above the same seeds' N=128 12000-step values (0.193 / 0.197). Force gained only 0.019 and 0.007 between steps 6000 and 12000. accel_step plateaued at margins of 0.159 / 0.154, with headroom-normalised margins of 0.76 and 0.65, inside the predicted [0.62, 0.77]. So the N=64 force ceiling sits above N=128, and accel_step stays flat whatever the training length or N.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds meet every expected-if-true criterion: final force >= 0.23, at least 0.03 above N=128, 6000->12000 gain <= 0.04, and normalised accel_step inside [0.62, 0.77]. The step-3000 force margins (0.200 / 0.236) differ from the 3000-step runs (0.215 / 0.261) by 0.015 / 0.025. Both are inside the 0.03 tolerance, but seed 21 is close to it, so cross-length comparisons still carry some horizon risk. Neither N has fully levelled off: N=64 still gains about 0.001-0.003 per 1000 steps and N=128 about 0.003-0.005. In seed 21 the N=64 minus N=128 gap shrank from 0.091 at step 6000 to 0.069 at step 12000 (seed 20 held steady at 0.062). A much longer run could therefore narrow the gap further. Training to 24000 steps with N=128 reaching within 0.015 of N=64 would turn this into a growth-rate effect. The force signal sits at layer 1 (distance margin 0.72 / 0.57) and has not been tested against distance regressed out, so this is a 'force-decodability ceiling' and not evidence of a separate force representation. Only two seeds and one data_seed were used.
